Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2 \times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PBP^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\color{red}\lambda_1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${\color{red}{\mathbf{v}_1}},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\color{blue}\lambda_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\lambda}_{\color{blue}3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{blue}3},$ then $A=PBP^{-1},$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14245038/assets/8668443119fd2ed6fd6994fc9d70a91a33c58e905e1efe6f7fcace1d62958883.svg)
Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14245038/assets/e5138ea7a633b391f344122e68170e9b0b6bad37b44e6d77be9fa5dc9ce65309.svg)
we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\color{blue}\lambda_{1,2}=1 \pm 3\textrm{i}}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\color{red}\lambda_3=-3}.$
